user_story: As a registered customer, I want to log in to the Sauce Demo store at https://www.saucedemo.com so that I can reach the product catalogue. Acceptance criteria: the login form has a username field [data-test="username"], a password field [data-test="password"] and a login button [data-test="login-button"]; logging in with username 'standard_user' and password 'secret_sauce' redirects to a URL containing '/inventory.html' and shows the page title element '.title' with the text 'Products'.

As a locked-out customer, I want a clear error message when I try to log in at https://www.saucedemo.com so that I understand why access is denied. Acceptance criteria: logging in with username 'locked_out_user' and password 'secret_sauce' keeps me on the login page and shows the error container [data-test="error"] with text containing 'Sorry, this user has been locked out'.

As a signed-in customer on https://www.saucedemo.com, I want to log out from the side menu so that my session ends securely. Acceptance criteria: after logging in with 'standard_user' / 'secret_sauce', clicking the burger menu button '#react-burger-menu-btn' opens the side menu, clicking the logout link '#logout_sidebar_link' returns me to the login page, and the login button [data-test="login-button"] is visible again.

As a visitor to https://www.saucedemo.com, I want the login form to validate required fields so that I know what is missing. Acceptance criteria: clicking the login button [data-test="login-button"] with both fields empty shows the error container [data-test="error"] with text containing 'Username is required'; entering only username 'standard_user' and clicking login shows an error containing 'Password is required'.

As a customer browsing https://www.saucedemo.com, I want the product list to display complete product cards so that I can compare items. Acceptance criteria: after logging in with 'standard_user' / 'secret_sauce', the inventory page shows exactly 6 product cards '.inventory_item'; every card contains a name element '.inventory_item_name' with non-empty text and a price element '.inventory_item_price' whose text starts with '$'.

As a customer on https://www.saucedemo.com, I want to sort products by price so that I can find the cheapest item first. Acceptance criteria: after logging in with 'standard_user' / 'secret_sauce', selecting the option with value 'lohi' in the sort dropdown [data-test="product-sort-container"] reorders the list so that the numeric values of the '.inventory_item_price' elements appear in ascending order.

As a customer on https://www.saucedemo.com, I want to add and remove a product from my cart so that the cart badge stays accurate. Acceptance criteria: after logging in with 'standard_user' / 'secret_sauce', clicking [data-test="add-to-cart-sauce-labs-backpack"] makes the cart badge '.shopping_cart_badge' show '1' and the button label change to 'Remove'; clicking [data-test="remove-sauce-labs-backpack"] removes the badge from the page.

As a customer on https://www.saucedemo.com, I want to complete a full checkout so that my order is confirmed. Acceptance criteria: after logging in with 'standard_user' / 'secret_sauce' and adding the backpack via [data-test="add-to-cart-sauce-labs-backpack"], clicking the cart link '.shopping_cart_link' then [data-test="checkout"] opens the information form; filling [data-test="firstName"] with 'Saif', [data-test="lastName"] with 'Afzal', [data-test="postalCode"] with '201301' and clicking [data-test="continue"] shows the overview page with an item total; clicking [data-test="finish"] shows the confirmation header '.complete-header' with text 'Thank you for your order!'.

As a customer checking out on https://www.saucedemo.com, I want the checkout information form to enforce required fields so that my order has complete delivery data. Acceptance criteria: after logging in with 'standard_user' / 'secret_sauce', adding the backpack via [data-test="add-to-cart-sauce-labs-backpack"], opening the cart '.shopping_cart_link' and clicking [data-test="checkout"], filling only [data-test="firstName"] with 'Saif' and [data-test="lastName"] with 'Afzal' and clicking [data-test="continue"] shows the error container [data-test="error"] with text containing 'Postal Code is required'.

As a customer on https://www.saucedemo.com, I want to open a product's detail page and return to the catalogue so that I can keep browsing. Acceptance criteria: after logging in with 'standard_user' / 'secret_sauce', clicking the first product name '.inventory_item_name' navigates to a URL containing 'inventory-item.html'; clicking the back button [data-test="back-to-products"] returns to a URL containing '/inventory.html' with the '.title' element showing 'Products'.

As a mobile customer, I want the Sauce Demo store at https://www.saucedemo.com to remain usable on a small screen so that I can shop from my phone. Acceptance criteria: with the viewport set to 375x812 (mobile portrait), logging in with 'standard_user' / 'secret_sauce' shows the inventory page; the burger menu button '#react-burger-menu-btn' is visible at this viewport and clicking it opens the side menu container '.bm-menu' with the logout link '#logout_sidebar_link' visible inside it.

As a screen-reader user, I want product images and login fields on https://www.saucedemo.com to carry accessible attributes so that assistive technology can describe them. Acceptance criteria: the login fields [data-test="username"] and [data-test="password"] each have a non-empty 'placeholder' attribute; after logging in with 'standard_user' / 'secret_sauce', every product image inside '.inventory_item' ('img.inventory_item_img') has a non-empty 'alt' attribute.

As a returning user, I want to log in to the secure area at https://the-internet.herokuapp.com/login so that I can access protected content. Acceptance criteria: the form has fields '#username' and '#password' and a submit button 'button[type="submit"]'; logging in with username 'tomsmith' and password 'SuperSecretPassword!' navigates to a URL containing '/secure' and shows the flash banner '.flash.success' with text containing 'You logged into a secure area!'.

As a user who mistyped my password, I want a clear failure message at https://the-internet.herokuapp.com/login so that I can correct it. Acceptance criteria: submitting username 'tomsmith' with wrong password 'wrongpassword' via '#username', '#password' and 'button[type="submit"]' keeps me on the login page and shows the flash banner '.flash.error' with text containing 'Your password is invalid!'.

As a user of the element manager at https://the-internet.herokuapp.com/add_remove_elements/, I want to add and delete elements so that the list reflects my actions. Acceptance criteria: clicking the 'Add Element' button (button[onclick="addElement()"]) twice creates two delete buttons '.added-manually'; clicking one delete button leaves exactly one '.added-manually' button on the page.

As a user on https://the-internet.herokuapp.com/javascript_alerts, I want to confirm a JavaScript dialog so that my choice is recorded. Acceptance criteria: clicking the button with text 'Click for JS Confirm' opens a native confirm dialog; accepting it makes the result element '#result' show 'You clicked: Ok'; dismissing it on a second attempt makes '#result' show 'You clicked: Cancel'.

As a user on https://the-internet.herokuapp.com/dynamic_loading/1, I want the page to reveal hidden content after an asynchronous wait so that I see the loaded result. Acceptance criteria: the '#finish' element is hidden initially; clicking the Start button ('#start button') shows a loading indicator '#loading'; after the loading indicator disappears, the '#finish' element becomes visible with the text 'Hello World!' (allow up to 10 seconds for the load to complete).

As a user on https://the-internet.herokuapp.com/upload, I want to upload a file so that the server confirms what it received. Acceptance criteria: selecting a small text file with the file input '#file-upload' and clicking the submit button '#file-submit' navigates to a page with the heading 'File Uploaded!' and shows the uploaded file's name inside '#uploaded-files'.

As a user on https://the-internet.herokuapp.com/checkboxes, I want checkbox states to change only when I toggle them so that the form reflects my choices. Acceptance criteria: the page has two 'input[type="checkbox"]' elements, the first initially unchecked and the second initially checked; checking the first makes both checked; unchecking the second leaves only the first checked.

As a user on https://the-internet.herokuapp.com/dropdown, I want to pick an option from the dropdown so that my selection is applied. Acceptance criteria: the select element '#dropdown' initially shows the disabled prompt 'Please select an option'; selecting the option with text 'Option 2' makes the select's value '2' and the 'Option 2' option becomes the selected one.

As a data reviewer on https://the-internet.herokuapp.com/tables, I want the example table to expose its rows and columns so that I can verify records. Acceptance criteria: table '#table1' has a header row containing the column headings 'Last Name', 'First Name', 'Email' and 'Due'; the table body contains 4 rows; one row contains the email 'jsmith@gmail.com' in the same row as the last name 'Smith'.

As a user on https://the-internet.herokuapp.com/notification_message_rendered, I want an on-screen notification after I trigger an action so that I get feedback. Acceptance criteria: clicking the 'Click here' link loads a new notification; the flash element '#flash' becomes visible and its text contains either 'Action successful' or 'Action unsuccessful'; the flash can be dismissed via its close icon '.close'.

As a visitor to https://the-internet.herokuapp.com, I want to navigate from the home page to an example page and back so that I can explore the catalogue of examples. Acceptance criteria: the home page shows the heading 'Welcome to the-internet'; clicking the link with text 'A/B Testing' navigates to a URL containing '/abtest' and shows an 'h3' heading; navigating back returns to the home page with the 'Available Examples' heading visible.

As a tester on https://the-internet.herokuapp.com/status_codes, I want to verify how the site reports HTTP status codes so that response handling can be checked end to end. Acceptance criteria: clicking the link with text '200' navigates to a URL containing '/status_codes/200' and the page body text contains 'This page returned a 200 status code'; returning to /status_codes and clicking the link with text '404' shows body text containing 'This page returned a 404 status code'.
